Solution 1 is the only one with a checkable derivation, and its algebra holds up. Substituting $z = 2u/(d+u)$ into the boundary-condition recurrence gives $u^3-(2d-3)u^2+d(d-2)u-d^2=0$, which factors as $(u-d)(u^2+(3-d)u+d)=0$. The quadratic's discriminant is $(d-1)(d-9)$, so a real bound-state root appears exactly when $d \ge 9$, and $d=9$ gives $s_1=3<s_0\approx 3.343$. That makes $d_c=8$, given its transition-rate model. I did not independently verify that model, so this rests on the internal consistency of the derivation.

Solutions 2 and 3 do not have a derivation that supports their thresholds. Solution 2's $(d-1)/4=1$ criterion is an ad hoc second-moment heuristic, and Solution 3's choice of $d_c=3$ is asserted rather than derived.

CHOICE: 1
